description: Biomanufacturing can produce materials foods and therapeutics but requires scale governance and sustainability analysis.
Genomic and biosurveillance systems can support preparedness but require trust privacy and international cooperation.
Advanced therapies can be transformative but remain expensive and hard to scale equitably.
Crop and microbial biotechnology may support food resilience but raises farmer autonomy and ecological questions.
Programmable biological design can support medicine manufacturing sensing and climate applications.
Environmental biotechnology may support remediation and monitoring but requires ecological caution.
AI can accelerate biological discovery and design while increasing validation and dual-use governance needs.
Genome editing has major therapeutic promise but raises access safety and heritable ethics concerns.
